nodes.name: Ce-PBA coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: 3.0 mmol CeCl₃ and 5.0 g PVP10 are added to a mixture of 50 mL ethanol and 25 mL deionized water. Then, 0.6593 g K₃Fe(CN)₆ is added to 40 mL of deionized water. Finally, the solution is mixed and stirred for 20 min. Subsequently, transfer the mixture to a vacuum oven at 25°C and continue the reaction for 12 h. After the reaction is complete, wash the product with ethanol and deionized water, centrifuge, dry it in a vacuum oven at 60°C, and finally the Ce-PBA is collected. At the same time, keeping other conditions unchanged, the mass of PVP used is 3.0 and 8.0 g to obtain Ce-PBA-3 and Ce-PBA-8, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ce-PBA ... At the same time, keeping other conditions unchanged, the mass of PVP used is 3.0 and 8.0 g...

nodes.name: Ce-PBA-250 calcination
nodes.procedure: Take 0.5 g Ce-PBA and place it in a ceramic boat, then place the boat in a tube furnace for calcination. The calcination conditions are as follows: the temperature is raised to 250°C at a rate of 2°C min⁻¹ in a nitrogen atmosphere, and then held at that temperature for 3 h.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ce-PBA-250 ... temperature is raised to 250°C at a rate of 2°C min⁻¹...

nodes.name: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1 phosphating
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g Ce-PBA powder is mixed with 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂ particles and shaken to make them evenly mixed. The mixture is subsequently placed in a ceramic boat and the ceramic boat is placed in a tube furnace for calcination. And the temperature is raised to 250°C at a rate of 2°C min⁻¹ in a nitrogen atmosphere, and then held at that temperature for 3 h. After waiting for tubular furnace cooling to room temperature, washing the solid with deionized water and ethanol and drying in vacuum oven at 60°C.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1 ... 0.5 g Ce-PBA powder is mixed with 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂...

nodes.name: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 phosphating
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g Ce-PBA-250 powder and 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂ particles are weighed, respectively, and they are mixed and shaken to make them mixed uniformly. Next, the mixture is calcined in a ceramic boat. The calcination conditions are same as those used to prepare CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1. Until the tube furnace cooling to room temperature, washing them with deionized water and ethanol and drying in vacuum oven at 60°C and CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 is obtained.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 ... 0.5 g Ce-PBA-250 powder and 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂ particles...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce-PBA exhibits layered hexagonal morphology size ~5-10 μm. CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 shows irregular nanoparticles composed of stacked nanofragments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1, under the influence of PVP, Ce³⁺ and Fe(CN)₆³⁻ occur co-precipitation reaction... the formation of Ce-PBA with a size of approximately 5-10 μm (Fig. 1(a, b) and S1)... Ce-PBA-250 is decomposed completely into irregular nanoparticles after low temperature phosphatization (Fig. 1(c, d)).

nodes.characterization_summary: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 shows lattice fringes 0.376 nm (110), 0.245 nm (210) of Ce-PBA and 0.287 nm (021), 0.316 nm (002) of CePO₄ with distinct heterointerfaces. Amorphous regions observed on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1(g) presents a high-resolution TEM image of CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2, where lattice fringes with spacing of 0.376 nm and 0.245 nm correspond to the (110) and (210) crystal planes of Ce-PBA, while lattice fringes with spacing of 0.287 nm and 0.316 nm correspond to the (021) and (002) crystal planes of CePO₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 shows diffuse rings confirming amorphous phase with faint diffraction rings for CePO₄ (012, 320) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction pattern of CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 mainly exhibits diffuse rings, once again confirming the existence of the amorphous phase...

nodes.characterization_summary: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 shows uniform distribution of C, N, O, Ce, Fe, P elements on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1(j1-j6) demonstrate the uniform distribution of C, N, O, Ce, Fe, and P elements on the surface of CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce-PBA-250 retains Ce-PBA peaks with reduced crystallinity. CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 shows Ce-PBA peaks plus new CePO₄ peaks with weaker crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2(a) shows the XRD patterns. After low-temperature calcination, Ce-PBA-250 still retains the characteristic peaks of Ce-PBA, but the crystallinity is reduced...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce-PBA-250, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 show C≡N stretch at 2077 cm⁻¹. PO₄³⁻ peaks at 1055 cm⁻¹ and 536 cm⁻¹ in CePO₄/Ce-PBA samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption peak observed at 2077 cm⁻¹ in Ce-PBA-250, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1, and CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 can be attributed to the stretching vibration of C≡N...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce-PBA completely decomposes at 340°C. Ce-PBA-250 shows higher weight loss rate confirming unstable structure. CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 has higher weight loss than CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1 before 340°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2(c) and 2(d) present the thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) of the different samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface areas: Ce-PBA 20.5 m²/g, Ce-PBA-250 20.3 m²/g, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1 32.8 m²/g, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 36.1 m²/g. CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 pore sizes uniformly distributed 0-35 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms, the specific surface areas of Ce-PBA, Ce-PBA-250, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1, and CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 are 20.5, 20.3, 32.8, and 36.1 m²g⁻¹, respectively (Fig. 2(e) and S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce-PBA-250 I_D/I_G = 0.92, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-1 = 0.93, CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2 = 0.98 indicating increasing defective carbon content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The D and G bands are not observed in Ce-PBA, but appeared in Ce-PBA-250, with an I_D/I_G ratio of 0.92.

nodes.characterization_summary: CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2: N 1s at 402.3 eV (Graphitic-N), 399.7 eV (Ce/Fe-N), 397.7 eV (C≡N); P 2p at 133.7 eV (P-O), 130.2 eV (P 2p₁/₂); Ce 3d shows Ce³⁺ (904.6, 886.3 eV) and Ce⁴⁺ (901.0, 882.7 eV); Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ with peak shifts indicating CePO₄-CePBA synergy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3(a-d) is the high-resolution XPS spectra of N 1s, P 2p, Ce 3d, and Fe 2p for CePO₄/Ce-PBA-2. The characteristic peak at 402.3, 399.7, and 397.7 eV corresponds to the Graphitic-N, Ce/Fe-N, and C≡N bond...
